claims.text: The homogenized Al0.7CoCrFeNi alloy initially has a dual-phase FCC/B2 lamellar structure.
The initial FCC/B2 interfaces are incoherent.
Stress concentration at the incoherent interfaces makes the initial alloy strong but brittle.
Treatment at 6 GPa and 1473 K for 2 hours will transform the lamellar topology into a hierarchical patterned microstructure.
The HPHT treatment will convert incoherent FCC/B2 interfaces into coherent interfaces.
The coherent interfaces form through pressure-assisted atomic rearrangement and diffusion.
Coherent lamellar interfaces permit dislocations to pass or shear across phase boundaries.
Dislocation transfer across coherent interfaces alleviates local stress concentration and prevents crack formation.
Coherent FCC/B2 interfaces will enable simultaneous dislocation slip, stacking-fault formation, and twinning in the treated alloy.
The activated deformation mechanisms will produce a homogeneous strain distribution between the FCC and B2 phases.
The GND densities of the FCC and B2 phases will converge at high strain after HPHT treatment.
The treated sample will exhibit elongated crack morphologies on its fracture surface.
Elongated fracture-surface cracks are an indicator of increased ductility in this alloy.
The untreated baseline exhibits isolated microcracks on its fracture surface.
The HPHT-treated alloy will have significantly improved ductility without loss of strength relative to the untreated baseline.
The proposed transformation occurs only below the pressure-temperature threshold for phase decomposition, instability, or melting.
Conventional thermal-mechanical treatment without high pressure will not produce the same hierarchical interface coherence.
The critical pressure and kinetics for the proposed transformation in Al0.7CoCrFeNi have not been empirically established by the cited evidence.
